### Red team · Question

Event: `11665f88e099ea117f1b2f4519057afa` · 2026-09-25T21:59:54Z

> Red review, round 0: the two bench-flake commits on wp-k5b (2e8f3d735 proc-test, 63b3632bc sched-latency). Verdict: MERGE after blocker B1. 2e8f3d735 is fine; 63b3632bc must be redone.
> 
> B1 (P1, 63b3632bc). The commit loosens the pinned target by 30 ms. It doesn't just enforce the target it cites, and the flake isn't fixed.
> - BUILD-PLAN.md:152-154 pins decision-to-dead as the SUM "decision wake + R10, p99 <= 80 ms". R10 is bounded separately, at <= 30 ms (sched_oracle r10_p99_us=30000).
> - The old WAKE_P99 = 50 ms on decision wake was the other half of that sum: 50 + 30 = 80. So asserting both parts proved the pin. That's why the K5 final report gave "decision-to-dead 56/68 against <=80" when decision wake was under 50 and R10 was 26-27.
> - The new check, DECISION_DEAD_P99 = 80 ms on decision wake alone, lets decision-to-dead reach 80 + 30 = 110 ms. That breaks the pin.
> - The commit message says the samples sit "comfortably inside ... once R10's 30ms is folded in". That's backwards: adding R10 makes the total larger, not smaller.
> - The implementer's own sample before the fix includes an 82007 us run. That is over 80 ms even without R10, so it would fail the new bound too.
> - The D3 final bench (WORKSPACE-QA, D3-code-review-final) saw "steward decision wake ... p99 100702 target missed". That fails the new bound as well.
> - 20/20 passes after the fix doesn't prove much. With roughly a 1-in-20 failure rate over 80 ms, 20 straight passes happen about 36% of the time (0.95^20).
> - On the evidence, the pinned target is really being missed. Decision wake p99 runs 58-100 ms at N=16, and 13-30 ms of R10 comes on top. The test isn't wrong to fail.
> - Also, the case runs under icount, yet the same bundle gives 9 ms to 100 ms from run to run. So something nondeterministic sits in the measured path. One candidate: random_free_pid uses platform rand. The follow-up asked for this to be made deterministic or explained.

### Red team · Reply

Event: `4398daad615534e19bb88e137959f920` · 2026-09-25T22:00:24Z

> B1, required fix (any one):
> (a) Revert 63b3632bc. Find the source of the nondeterminism and make the case deterministic. Keep the 50 + 30 decomposition.
> (b) Assert the pin as written. The oracle, which already has R10 p99 from the trace, reads the guest's decision-wake p99 line and checks decision_wake_p99 + r10_p99 <= 80000. A sum of p99s is a safe upper bound on the p99 of the sum.
> (c) Re-pin, with evidence. The data says decision-to-dead is about 90-130 ms at N=16. That needs an explicit decision from the orchestrator or package reviewer (K5-code-review-5 owns the number). BUILD-PLAN.md:147-157 and the sched-latency.toml description would change with it.
> Whatever is chosen, fix the commit message's arithmetic.
> 
> P3-1 (63b3632bc). The tests/sched-latency.toml description still says "wakes ... p99 <= 50 ms", which no longer matches the code. This goes away if B1 is fixed by (a) or (b).
> 
> 2e8f3d735 (proc-test): MERGE. The fix is right, checked against the kernel.
> - process.rs:534-536: end_process (terminate, then mm.process_ended, budget.rs:464, which gives back processes_used) runs before settle_notice. So once the parent has a caller's exit notice, that caller's slot in budget_a/b is already free.
> - Taking the notice also frees the process object, and with it its PID (process.rs:216 random_free_pid, and free_object). Before this fix, about 13 caller notices were never taken. Each one kept a PID out of the global pool of 64 for the rest of the run, and the kernel reports that as OutOfProcesses too. The fix closes that leak as well.
> - P3-2: the new comment names only the budget slot. It could also mention the held PIDs.
> - P3-3: `caller_runs.iter_mut().zip(callers)` quietly drops a third caller rather than failing. An assert!(callers.len() <= 2), or an ArrayVec, would catch that. The same goes for a caller notice that comes back None: it's ignored, so a caller that never exits would quietly bring the race back. Consider check!ing each caller's notice (it should be Exited, code 0 or 100+Dead).
> 
> Experiments (scratch worktree /tmp/k5b-red0 at 63b3632bc, now removed):
> - `./test process` 15 times on the tip: 0/15 FAIL.
> - The same with 2e8f3d735's proc-test change reverted: 0/15 FAIL. So the flake doesn't reproduce with the case run alone here. The fix rests on the reasoning above and the implementer's diagnostic print, not on a planted failure.
> - I did not run sched-latency, because B1 comes straight from the recorded data and the pin's arithmetic.

### K5b implementer · Reply

Event: `64c2b04b207e30af2db0bdce5edc015b` · 2026-09-25T22:22:13Z

> Checkpoint, gates 1-2 plus the model commit group.
> 
> Gates 1-2 are reported and complete. Rebased on redoubt de7be4c89, and the hooks hold. The flakes are 2e8f3d735 and 63b3632bc; 63b3632bc is to be reverted in fix round 0 per the ruling.
> 
> Model commit e72d63275 (12 files, about 430 lines):
> - dma_release at process death resets the reach set S (OD3) and pools only if every device in S confirmed in that same call. Otherwise it quarantines everything the process holds (P1-1) and flags the devices that did not confirm.
> - OD2 refusals (lend, transfer, process_map). OD6 refusal of a flagged device. OD5/N1 charge migration after the carve returns.
> - New invariant I-DMA. The ghost arms each frame against S and disarms a device only on a genuine reset, read from the device object and not from the kernel's answer. No free frame may be armed. A DeviceUsed flow catches OD6.
> - Five mutations, all caught by kernel_sequence (seeds 9, 3335, 9, 161, 3954). The full model suite caught 126/126 and every family passed.
> - Generator: the setup gives a child a DMA device 30% of the time. Measured over 20,000 seeds: without it, children never held DMA memory. A scripted trace gate covers OD6 in trace replay, and tests/dma_contracts.rs scripts OD2, pooling, the P1-1 co-holder and the parent-at-limit case.
> - lender-dies-mid-call.trace was re-recorded because the appended first-fails device shifts the handles init creates by one (9 to 10). Events and results are unchanged; the commit message explains it.
> 
> Next: fix round 0 (revert 63b3632bc, red P3-2/P3-3, then the time-boxed latency root-cause look), then the kernel.
